audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Unbound is attributed to Yone's Q in whys[3] ("His Q Soul Unbound dash pattern") and wants.foe[0] ("Use Q Soul Unbound to dash through or past you"), and content.early describes "a Q dash that requires him to walk back to his body".
audit.why: Soul Unbound is Yone's E. His Q is Mortal Steel, a 4s thrust whose third cast dashes and knocks up. The body-rewind belongs only to E. This matters because the two have completely different cooldowns and completely different punish windows: Mortal Steel is back in 4 seconds and is not a window at all, whereas Soul Unbound is 22/19/16/13/10s and IS the window where Yone cannot escape a three-stack commit. Merging them means the player never learns which cooldown to count.
audit.corrected: E Soul Unbound = spirit leaves body, rewinds on expiry, 22/19/16/13/10s. Q Mortal Steel = 4s, third cast dashes and knocks up.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fate Sealed is called a knockup throughout — "His R knockup can interrupt your Devour attempt" (mid, whys[4]), "respect the knockup angle" (spikes[1].text), "if he tries to knock up your backline" (late).
audit.why: Fate Sealed blinks Yone behind the last champion in a line and PULLS everyone hit toward him. It carries no knockup and the kit flags it dash-only. The difference is not cosmetic for a Tahm Kench: a pull drags your carries into Yone rather than launching them, so the peel answer is to body-block the line and Devour, not to brace for airborne. It also means Yone's R is not a knockup you can chain your own displacement off.
audit.corrected: Fate Sealed pulls everyone in the line toward him, cooldown 120/100/80s. The only knockup in Yone's kit is the third Mortal Steel cast.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer correctly identifies Soul Unbound as the matchup-defining cooldown but never states it, and no line in either layer carries a number for any of Yone's abilities.
audit.why: Soul Unbound is 22 seconds at rank 1 and still 10 at rank 5 — by far the longest cooldown in his laning kit and the only one that is a genuine punish window. Spirit Cleave is 14s and Fate Sealed is 120/100/80s. Without those figures "track it before every engage" gives the player nothing to count.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2], whys[5], spikes[0].text, wants.you[0], tradeGood and dosFull[1].d all describe a "stun into Devour" / "stun-Devour" sequence off one set of three stacks.
audit.why: Riot's Tongue Lash text: at 3 stacks "they are stunned and the stacks are consumed". Riot's passive: three stacks are the requirement to Devour. They are alternative spenders of one charge. The level 2-3 window this matchup is built around is exactly where the mistake is costly — the player lands his third stack, throws a fourth Q for the stun, and discovers his ultimate is greyed out on a champion who then E-rewinds away.
audit.corrected: Land the third stack and then Devour. Do not throw a fourth Tongue Lash first.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (Riot Data Dragon 16.15.1) — P and Q descriptions

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid says "Abyssal Voyage also opens global teleport threat".
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is Tahm Kench's removed pre-2020 W. The current W is Abyssal Dive, a 1000-1200 range knockup on 21/20/19/18/17s, with no global component. The advice to plan level-6 macro around a global that does not exist is actively misleading.
audit.corrected: No global in the kit; level 6 is Devour. Ping the jungler for the dive instead.

audit.why: 51.23% over 1300 games with Tahm Kench taking the first three stages, skill in the middle and Yone taking two-plus items. That matches a lane won early and lost to scaling, and it matches the phase text; no reconciliation needed.

edits.before: At level 1 your Tongue Lash range gives you the CS battle — slow him off the wave every time he steps up to last-hit, and let the passive stack accrue without overcommitting. He has no escape tool yet, just a Q dash that requires him to walk back to his body, so a level 1 Tongue Lash that tags him twice sets up a clean level 2 all-in. Levels 2-3 are your best window: land Tongue Lash, auto twice, and when the third stack locks in hit Devour — he cannot E spirit-rewind out of an active Devour cast and he has no armor items to eat the bonus damage. Make him burn Flash or respawn in fountain before this window closes.
edits.after: At level 1 your Tongue Lash range gives you the CS battle — slow him off the wave every time he steps up to last-hit, and let the passive stack accrue without overcommitting. The ability that snaps him back to his body is Soul Unbound, his E and not his Q, so a level 1 Tongue Lash that tags him twice sets up a clean level 2 all-in. Levels 2-3 are your best window: land Tongue Lash, auto twice, and when the third stack locks in hit Devour rather than a fourth Q, because that stun would consume all three stacks. Make him burn Flash or respawn in fountain before this window closes.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are where you respect his kit rather than press. Yone's Q dash pattern lets him trade in, dash out, and re-enter with his second Q before your stacks reset, so if you miss Tongue Lash he gets a free trade and walks away healthy. Play for CS and stack fishing with Q poke, not full commits. At level 6 neither of you wins a clean all-in — his R knockup can interrupt your Devour attempt if he lands it first, so bait his R by walking in aggressively, then sidestep the angle and punish the cooldown with a full stack combo. Abyssal Voyage also opens global teleport threat, so pin your jungler for a dive setup rather than solo-forcing it.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are where you respect his kit rather than press. Yone's Q dash pattern lets him trade in, dash out, and re-enter with his second Q before your stacks reset, so if you miss Tongue Lash he gets a free trade and walks away healthy. Play for CS and stack fishing with Q poke, not full commits. At level 6 neither of you wins a clean all-in — Fate Sealed pulls everyone it hits toward him rather than knocking up, so bait it by walking in aggressively, sidestep the line, then punish a 120s cooldown at rank 1 with the full stack pattern. Ping your jungler for a dive setup rather than solo-forcing it.

edits.before: Once Yone has two items he becomes genuinely difficult to catch — his Q dashes and E spirit-rewind mean he controls the distance and your stacks bleed off before you can complete the combo without Flash. Your job shifts: use Tongue Lash to zone him off your carries in teamfights rather than chasing a solo kill, and Devour him out of his R wind-up if he tries to knock up your backline. You still win the objective-control and peel game decisively at this stage, but do not chase him in the sidelane — he will run the clock on your stacks and punish the overextension with a double-Q burst you cannot Devour-tank alone.
edits.after: Once Yone has two items he becomes genuinely difficult to catch — his Q dashes and E spirit-rewind mean he controls the distance and your stacks bleed off before you can complete the combo without Flash. Your job shifts: use Tongue Lash to zone him off your carries in teamfights rather than chasing a solo kill, and Devour him out of his R wind-up if he tries to pull your backline in. edits.before: A full three-stack stun into Devour at level 3 removes him from the fight entirely and deals bonus damage; his Q dash comes back while he is inside your belly, wasted.
edits.after: Three stacks is one charge — the Q stun eats all three, so spend them on Devour at level 3; his Mortal Steel dash ticks back up while he is inside your belly, wasted.

notes: The three suspectNames flagged in the packet for this matchup are all false positives. The two real errors — Soul Unbound attributed to Q, and Fate Sealed described as a knockup — are both slot/effect mistakes rather than misspellings, so name-distance checks cannot see them. A validator that cross-checks "<ability name> is his <slot>" against the kit, and one that checks knockup/pull/stun claims against the kit flags, would catch this whole class. I did NOT touch content.early's claim that Yone "cannot E spirit-rewind out of an active Devour cast" — whether suppression blocks the Soul Unbound snap-back is not answerable from Riot's text and belongs to the needsResearch set, so it needs a League Wiki check before it is either kept or removed.
